chunks: Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, he said: Ali ibn Ahmad al-Tabari narrated to us, he said: Abu Sa'id narrated to us, he said: Karrash narrated to us, he said: Anas narrated to us, he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Whoever gazes at the back of a woman until the size of her bones becomes clear to him from behind her clothes while he is fasting, he has broken his fast. - Meaning, he has conditioned himself for breaking the fast by what emanates from his desires and the inclinations of his ambition, so he becomes among those who risk committing sin. -
ai.seo_question: Does gazing at a woman's body break the fast of a Muslim?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration in *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* to illustrate how specific, deliberate visual scrutiny can nullify the fast, distinguishing it from casual glances. The commentary clarifies that the act 'conditions' the soul by intensifying internal desires (*nawazi' al-himma*), thereby creating a predisposition to major sin and breaking the spiritual integrity of the fast. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the internal state of intention and desire alongside physical actions in jurisprudence.
